Memphis-Egypt.name: Memphis
Memphis-Egypt.evidence_basis: EES drill-core survey (Jeffreys 2000; Love 2003) documents a 600 ha Mit Rahina core plus Memphite ribbon suburbs along the Saqqara-Abusir escarpment, yielding 64k-88.5k at Old and New Kingdom peaks at 120-150/ha over settled quarters (Kemp 2006; Butzer 1976).

Pi-Ramesses-Egypt.name: Pi-Ramesses
Pi-Ramesses-Egypt.evidence_basis: Magnetometry and Austrian-German excavations at Qantir (Pusch & Herold; Bietak 1996) reveal a 1,000-1,800 ha dispersed imperial capital with palaces, chariotry garrisons, and bronze foundries peaking near 79k before Pelusiac silting triggered abandonment c. 1060 BC.

Thebes-Egypt.name: Thebes
Thebes-Egypt.evidence_basis: East Bank Karnak-Luxor urban quarters (~380-450 ha) plus West Bank mortuary temple estates support an 18th-19th Dynasty peak of ~77.5k (Kemp 2006; Baines & Malek 2000), dropping sharply after Ashurbanipal's 663 BC sack.

Sais-Egypt.name: Sais
Sais-Egypt.evidence_basis: EES drill-core and geophysical surveys (Wilson 2006; 2011) indicate a ~3 km by 2 km western Delta royal capital under the 24th and 26th (Saite) Dynasties, peaking near 48.5k across ~280-320 ha of inhabited precincts.

Avaris-Egypt.name: Avaris
Avaris-Egypt.evidence_basis: Austrian Archaeological Institute excavations (Bietak 1996; Moeller 2016) map a ~250 ha Hyksos 15th Dynasty capital (~170/ha density = 42.5k), contracting after Ahmose I's conquest to the 18th Dynasty naval base of Perunefer.

Tanis-Egypt.name: Tanis
Tanis-Egypt.evidence_basis: French Mission excavations (Brissaud; Montet; Snape 2014) document a >=180 ha enclosed tell built with spolia from abandoned Pi-Ramesses as the 21st-22nd Dynasty northern capital, housing ~35k-40k at its TIP peak.

Itjtawy-Egypt.name: Itjtawy
Itjtawy-Egypt.evidence_basis: Middle Kingdom disembedded royal capital founded by Amenemhat I between the Lisht pyramids; satellite and coring surveys (Parcak; Arnold; Moeller 2016) indicate ~140-180 ha of court and administrative quarters peaking near 34.8k in the 12th Dynasty.

Bubastis-Egypt.name: Bubastis
Bubastis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Multi-mound tell of ~160-180 ha with Old/Middle Kingdom governor palaces and monumental 22nd Dynasty Bastet temples (Bakr; Lange-Athinodorou; Baines & Malek 2000) reaching ~34.6k as the Libyan 22nd Dynasty royal residence.

Amarna-Egypt.name: Amarna
Amarna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Kemp's EES mapping of ~350-450 ha of suburban villas, dense housing plots, and workmen's village plus agricultural carrying-capacity modeling (Kemp 2006; 2012) estimates 25k-35k during Akhenaten's brief 1348-1332 BC occupation prior to rapid abandonment.

Heliopolis-Egypt.name: Heliopolis
Heliopolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Egyptian-German excavations at Matariya (Raue; Ashmawy) reveal a ~1,100x900 m sacred precinct and extensive surrounding residential/industrial quarters (~150-200 ha) with Papyrus Harris I attesting 12,963 temple staff under Ramesses III.

Herakleopolis Magna-Egypt.name: Herakleopolis Magna
Herakleopolis Magna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Spanish Archaeological Mission excavations (Perez Die; Moeller 2016) document a ~130-150 ha tell controlling the Fayum entrance that peaked near 27.6k as the 9th-10th Dynasty royal capital and revived under 22nd-23rd Dynasty regional kings.

Hermopolis Magna-Egypt.name: Hermopolis Magna
Hermopolis Magna-Egypt.evidence_basis: British Museum excavations (A.J. Spencer 1983-1993) map a 1.5x1.0 km (~120-150 ha) tell serving as 15th Upper Egyptian nome capital and seat of King Nimlot during the Piye campaign (c. 728 BC), peaking near 26.9k.

Mendes-Egypt.name: Mendes
Mendes-Egypt.evidence_basis: Redford and Hansen excavations map ~100-140 ha across Tell el-Rub'a with Predynastic-Old Kingdom strata, harbor basins, and massive Late Period mud-brick temple enclosures (Snape 2014), scaling to ~24.2k in the Saite era.

Asyut-Egypt.name: Asyut
Asyut-Egypt.evidence_basis: 13th Upper Egyptian nome capital and Darb el-Arba'in caravan terminus whose monumental FIP-MK nomarchal tombs (Kahl; Butzer 1976) indicate a major provincial metropolis of ~16k-23.6k.

Akhmim-Egypt.name: Akhmim
Akhmim-Egypt.evidence_basis: 9th Upper Egyptian nome capital and Min cult center with vast El-Hawawish OK necropolis (>800 tombs, Kanawati) and monumental Ramesside temple precinct, supporting ~15k-19.6k at New Kingdom peak (Butzer 1976).

Giza-Egypt.name: Giza
Giza-Egypt.evidence_basis: AERA excavations at Heit el-Ghurab and east-plateau coring (Lehner 1997; 2015; Hawass 1996; Love 2003) document >7 ha of barracks, bakeries, and officials' quarters within a 200-300 ha settlement scatter housing ~18.8k during 4th Dynasty pyramid construction.

Crocodilopolis-Egypt.name: Crocodilopolis
Crocodilopolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Fayum provincial capital centered on a >10 ha Sobek temple precinct at Kiman Faris surrounded by ~80-100 ha of urban mounds; 12th Dynasty basin reclamation propelled its MK peak to ~18.6k (Butzer 1976; Baines & Malek 2000).

Athribis-Egypt.name: Athribis
Athribis-Egypt.evidence_basis: 10th Lower Egyptian nome capital at the central Delta apex excavated by the Polish-Egyptian mission (Mysliwiec; Snape 2014), expanding to ~18.4k under the 26th Dynasty when its regional princes held major Delta commands.

Coptos-Egypt.name: Coptos
Coptos-Egypt.evidence_basis: 5th Upper Egyptian nome capital and terminus of the Wadi Hammamat gold/Red Sea trade route; ~50-70 ha urban tell and Min temple complex (Petrie; Herbert & Berlin; Butzer 1976) supporting ~14k-17.4k in the New Kingdom.

Sebennytos-Egypt.name: Sebennytos
Sebennytos-Egypt.evidence_basis: 12th Lower Egyptian nome capital on the Damietta branch with Onuris-Shu temple precinct (Spencer Delta Survey; Snape 2014), growing steadily through the TIP and Saite Delta expansion to ~16.8k.

Dendera-Egypt.name: Dendera
Dendera-Egypt.evidence_basis: 6th Upper Egyptian nome capital and Hathor cult metropolis with extensive IFAO-mapped OK-FIP settlement strata and mastaba fields (~45-60 ha urban area, Marouard & Moeller 2016), peaking near 15.9k in the New Kingdom.

Buto-Egypt.name: Buto
Buto-Egypt.evidence_basis: DAI excavations (von der Way; Hartung) reveal a ~40-55 ha dual tell (Pe and Dep) serving as Predynastic/Early Dynastic Lower Egyptian center (~11.6k) and reviving as a major Saite cult and administrative city (~15.2k).

Leontopolis-Egypt.name: Leontopolis
Leontopolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Redmount and Friedman Berkeley survey maps a ~50-70 ha central Delta mound that served as 11th Lower Egyptian nome center and 23rd Dynasty regional royal seat under Iuput II, peaking near 14.9k in the TIP.

Abydos-Egypt.name: Abydos
Abydos-Egypt.evidence_basis: Penn-Yale-IFA excavations (Adams; Wegner 2001; Moeller 2016) document the ~15 ha Kom el-Sultan North Town plus the 12th Dynasty state-planned Wah-Sut town at South Abydos and Ramesside Osiris temple estate, peaking near 14.6k.

Xois-Egypt.name: Xois
Xois-Egypt.evidence_basis: 6th Lower Egyptian nome capital on an elevated central Delta gezira; Manetho places the 14th Dynasty regional kings here during the SIP (~12.9k), with EES Delta Survey material confirming continued expansion to ~14.2k in the Saite period.

Tell el-Balamun-Egypt.name: Tell el-Balamun
Tell el-Balamun-Egypt.evidence_basis: British Museum excavations (A.J. Spencer 1996-2009) map a ~80-100 ha northernmost 17th Lower Egyptian nome capital with massive 26th Dynasty Amun enclosure walls and fortress platform, peaking near 13.8k.

Thinis-Egypt.name: Thinis
Thinis-Egypt.evidence_basis: 8th Upper Egyptian nome capital and seat of the 1st-2nd Thinite Dynasties (Wilkinson 1999; Butzer 1976); its extensive Naga ed-Deir necropolis and regional agricultural basin support an Early Dynastic peak of ~13.6k and enduring provincial town of ~9k-11.6k.

Naukratis-Egypt.name: Naukratis
Naukratis-Egypt.evidence_basis: British Museum geophysical and surface survey (Villing et al. 2013-2019) doubled its known footprint to >60 ha on the Canopic branch, housing a cosmopolitan Greek-Egyptian emporium of ~12k-13.4k by the late Saite period.

Busiris-Egypt.name: Busiris
Busiris-Egypt.evidence_basis: 9th Lower Egyptian nome capital and principal northern Osiris cult center (EES Delta Survey; Snape 2014), serving as seat of a 22nd-24th Dynasty Meshwesh chiefdom and growing to ~13.3k in the Saite period.

Esna-Egypt.name: Esna
Esna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern 3rd Upper Egyptian nome urban center and Khnum cult town with extensive MK-NK cemeteries excavated by Downes and Garstang (Butzer 1976), eclipsing Elkab by the Late Period at ~12.6k.

Armant-Egypt.name: Armant
Armant-Egypt.evidence_basis: Original capital of the 4th Upper Egyptian nome and Montu cult seat excavated by Mond & Myers and IFAO (Thiers; Baines & Malek 2000), peaking near 11.5k in the 11th-12th Dynasties before Thebes assumed primary regional hegemony.

Thonis-Heracleion-Egypt.name: Thonis-Heracleion
Thonis-Heracleion-Egypt.evidence_basis: IEASM underwater excavations in Abu Qir Bay (Goddio & Fabre 2008) map a ~60-75 ha canalized island port, Amun-Gereb temple, and maritime customs emporium flourishing under the 26th Dynasty at ~11.4k.

Qaw el-Kebir-Egypt.name: Qaw el-Kebir
Qaw el-Kebir-Egypt.evidence_basis: 10th Upper Egyptian nome capital whose monumental 12th Dynasty terraced nomarchal tombs of Wahka I/II and Ibu (Petrie; Steckeweh; Butzer 1976) attest a major Middle Kingdom provincial city of ~11.2k.

Hermopolis Parva-Egypt.name: Hermopolis Parva
Hermopolis Parva-Egypt.evidence_basis: 7th Lower Egyptian nome administrative center on the western Canopic canal corridor (EES Delta Survey; Baines & Malek 2000), expanding strongly during the Saite western Delta boom to ~11.1k.

Oxyrhynchus-Egypt.name: Oxyrhynchus
Oxyrhynchus-Egypt.evidence_basis: 19th Upper Egyptian nome capital on the Bahr Yussef attested from New Kingdom onward with extensive Saite 26th Dynasty stone-lined tombs (Padro; Barcelona Mission), reaching ~10.8k by the Persian conquest.

Cusae-Egypt.name: Cusae
Cusae-Egypt.evidence_basis: 14th Upper Egyptian nome capital whose elite rock-cut necropolis at Meir (Blackman; Kanawati) and Carnarvon Tablet mention as the Hyksos-Theban border attest a substantial provincial hub of ~9.6k-10.5k.

Elkab-Egypt.name: Elkab
Elkab-Egypt.evidence_basis: Belgian Archaeological Mission excavations (Hendrickx; Claes; Moeller 2016) map an enclosed east-bank 3rd nome capital with inner OK-MK walled settlement and ~25 ha Late Period outer wall, peaking near 10.4k.

Atfih-Egypt.name: Atfih
Atfih-Egypt.evidence_basis: 22nd Upper Egyptian nome capital and sacred Hesat-cow Hathor cult town on the east bank south of Memphis (Butzer 1976; Baines & Malek 2000), growing to ~9.9k by the Saite period.

Hierakonpolis-Egypt.name: Hierakonpolis
Hierakonpolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Hierakonpolis Expedition surveys (Hoffman 1982; Friedman; Moeller 2016) trace a sprawling >25 ha Predynastic-Early Dynastic urban center (~8k-10k peak at unification) contracting gradually into a smaller walled Horus temple town by the New Kingdom.

Phakousa-Egypt.name: Phakousa
Phakousa-Egypt.evidence_basis: Eastern Delta nodal town on the Pelusiac branch just south of Avaris/Pi-Ramesses (EES Delta Survey; Bietak), absorbing regional trade after Qantir's decline and reaching ~9.6k in the Late Period.

Letopolis-Egypt.name: Letopolis
Letopolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: 2nd Lower Egyptian nome capital and Khenty-irty cult center at the western Delta apex (Jones 1995; Love 2003; Baines & Malek 2000), sustained by Memphite proximity and reaching ~9.4k under the Saite dynasty.

Edfu-Egypt.name: Edfu
Edfu-Egypt.evidence_basis: Oriental Institute excavations (Moeller 2016; Moeller & Marouard) reveal a deeply stratified 6-10 ha core tell with OK columned halls, SIP massive administrative grain silos, and dense housing supporting ~4.9k-8.9k.

Hu-Egypt.name: Hu
Hu-Egypt.evidence_basis: 7th Upper Egyptian nome capital at the Qena Bend excavated by Petrie (1901) and Bard (1994), showing continuous Predynastic through Late Period occupation across a major floodplain hub of ~7k-8.8k.

Elephantine-Egypt.name: Elephantine
Elephantine-Egypt.evidence_basis: DAI excavations (Kaiser; Seidlmayer 1996; von Pilgrim 1996; Moeller 2016) document a densely packed 10-15 ha First Cataract island city plus east-bank Syene quarry/trade suburb housing ~4.6k in the OK and ~7.9k-8.7k in the NK and Saite garrison eras.

Kom Ombo-Egypt.name: Kom Ombo
Kom Ombo-Egypt.evidence_basis: Strategic Nile bend settlement commanding Eastern Desert gold tracks and the Nubian approach; Austrian-Egyptian urban excavations (Forstner-Muller) reveal dense FIP-MK-NK-Late Period mudbrick quarters supporting ~6.8k-8.5k.

Imet-Egypt.name: Imet
Imet-Egypt.evidence_basis: 19th Lower Egyptian nome capital (Wadjet cult) 8.4 km NE of Pi-Ramesses excavated by Petrie (1888) and Manchester University (N. Rashed; EES Delta Survey), reaching ~8.46k in the Saite period.

Saft el-Hinna-Egypt.name: Saft el-Hinna
Saft el-Hinna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Capital of the 20th Lower Egyptian nome at the western entrance to Wadi Tumilat excavated by Naville (1887) and EES Delta Survey, serving as a major eastern frontier cult and administrative town of ~6.8k-8.4k.

Beni Hasan-Egypt.name: Beni Hasan
Beni Hasan-Egypt.evidence_basis: 16th Upper Egyptian nome seat under the powerful 11th-12th Dynasty Oryx nome nomarchs (Amenemhat, Khnumhotep II; Kanawati & Woods), whose vast rock-cut necropolis and lower-slope cemeteries indicate an MK peak near 8.35k.

Daphnae-Egypt.name: Daphnae
Daphnae-Egypt.evidence_basis: British Museum reinvestigation of Petrie's Pelusiac frontier fortress (Leclere & Spencer 2014) maps a ~35-45 ha fortified platform and urban surround garrisoned by Ionian and Carian mercenaries under Psamtik I (~7.4k-8.25k).

Lahun-Egypt.name: Lahun
Lahun-Egypt.evidence_basis: State-planned 12th Dynasty orthogonal pyramid town of Senusret II mapped by Petrie (9.5-14 ha walled enclosure, >250 small houses + 10 elite mansions; Kemp 2006; Moeller 2016) housing ~6k-7.85k during the late Middle Kingdom.

Kom Firin-Egypt.name: Kom Firin
Kom Firin-Egypt.evidence_basis: British Museum excavations (N. Spencer 2008; 2014) document a ~40-50 ha fortified western Delta town founded in the Ramesside Libyan-defense system with dense TIP-Saite domestic quarters supporting ~6.2k-7.75k.

Hardai-Egypt.name: Hardai
Hardai-Egypt.evidence_basis: 17th Upper Egyptian nome capital (Anubis cult) documented in Wilbour Papyrus landholdings and east-bank necropolis remains (Butzer 1976; Baines & Malek 2000), supporting ~6.2k-7.65k in the New Kingdom and Saite eras.

Malqata-Egypt.name: Malqata
Malqata-Egypt.evidence_basis: MMA and Waseda excavations (Kemp & O'Connor 1974; Lacovara) document a ~30 ha palace-city and ~80 ha complex beside Birket Habu built for Amenhotep III's Sed festivals, peaking near 7.25k before declining after his reign.

Tell el-Maskhuta-Egypt.name: Tell el-Maskhuta
Tell el-Maskhuta-Egypt.evidence_basis: University of Toronto excavations (Holladay 1982; Paice) reveal an unfortified SIP Hyksos village (~2.85k), long hiatus, and major Saite refoundation under Necho II c. 610 BC as a ~25-30 ha fortified canal-depot town (~6.85k).

Naqada-Egypt.name: Naqada
Naqada-Egypt.evidence_basis: Predynastic proto-urban center (~25-30 ha South Town and massive cemeteries excavated by Petrie, Kemp, and Bard 1994) peaking near 6.8k at unification before moderating to a regional Seth temple town of ~3k-4.4k.

Zawiyet Sultan-Egypt.name: Zawiyet Sultan
Zawiyet Sultan-Egypt.evidence_basis: Cologne-Cambridge survey (Bussmann; Moeller 2016) documents a ~30 ha provincial town mound with a 3rd Dynasty small step pyramid and 6th Dynasty elite rock-cut tombs, peaking near 6.75k in the Old Kingdom.

Shashotep-Egypt.name: Shashotep
Shashotep-Egypt.evidence_basis: 11th Upper Egyptian nome capital (Khnum cult) and associated Rifeh necropolis excavated by Petrie (1907), sustaining a mid-tier Middle Egyptian town of ~4.6k-6.55k (Butzer 1976).

Deir el-Ballas-Egypt.name: Deir el-Ballas
Deir el-Ballas-Egypt.evidence_basis: Reisner and Lacovara (1997; Moeller 2016) map a ~50 ha 17th-early 18th Dynasty forward campaign city with North/South Palaces, elite villas, and workmen's village peaking near 6.45k during the Hyksos wars before swift abandonment.

Abusir-Egypt.name: Abusir
Abusir-Egypt.evidence_basis: Czech Institute and EES coring (Verner 2002; Jeffreys 1997; Love 2003) identify an Early Dynastic valley settlement and prosperous 5th Dynasty pyramid-town cluster serving Sahure, Neferirkare, and Niuserre (~6.38k peak), reviving in the Saite necropolis era.

Sharuna-Egypt.name: Sharuna
Sharuna-Egypt.evidence_basis: Tubingen University excavations (Schenkel & Goma'a) document the 18th Upper Egyptian nome capital on the east bank with 6th Dynasty elite tombs and large Late Period tell strata supporting ~4.85k-6.25k.

Qus-Egypt.name: Qus
Qus-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern 5th Upper Egyptian nome town controlling the secondary Eastern Desert road to the Red Sea (Baines & Malek 2000; Butzer 1976), growing steadily from MK through Saite times to ~6.2k.

Pelusium-Egypt.name: Pelusium
Pelusium-Egypt.evidence_basis: Easternmost fortress-port at the Pelusiac mouth of the Nile (Valbelle & Carrez-Maratray; Snape 2014), rising during the TIP and Saite periods as Egypt's key Levantine gateway (~6.15k before Cambyses' 525 BC battle).

El-Hiba-Egypt.name: El-Hiba
El-Hiba-Egypt.evidence_basis: UC Berkeley excavations (Redmount; Wenke 1984) map a ~35-45 ha fortified hilltop town with massive 21st Dynasty mudbrick enclosure walls built by the High Priests of Amun to guard Middle Egypt's northern border (~6.1k peak).

Gebelein-Egypt.name: Gebelein
Gebelein-Egypt.evidence_basis: Italian and Polish surveys (Fiore Marochetti; Ejsmond) document a Predynastic-FIP-MK strategic river-narrows settlement with Hathor temple and Nubian mercenary garrison stelae, peaking near 5.65k in the FIP/MK.

Akoris-Egypt.name: Akoris
Akoris-Egypt.evidence_basis: Tsukuba University excavations (Kawanishi & Tsujimura) reveal an OK necropolis town (Fraser Tombs) and heavily fortified TIP Nile fortress-port controlling Middle Egypt's river traffic (~5.55k peak).

Gurob-Egypt.name: Gurob
Gurob-Egypt.evidence_basis: Petrie (1890) and Liverpool-Copenhagen excavations (Shaw 2008-2016) map a ~25 ha 18th-19th Dynasty royal harem-palace and linen-manufacturing town at the Fayum mouth, peaking near 5.48k under Amenhotep III-Ramesses II.

Aniba-Egypt.name: Aniba
Aniba-Egypt.evidence_basis: Steindorff (1937) and Smith (2003) document an ~8 ha walled Middle Kingdom fortress expanded into a larger unfortified New Kingdom viceregal capital of Wawat (Lower Nubia), housing ~5.38k at 18th-19th Dynasty height.

Tell Hebua-Egypt.name: Tell Hebua
Tell Hebua-Egypt.evidence_basis: SCA excavations (Abd el-Maksoud 1998-2015) uncover a massive multi-walled frontier fortress-town (Hebua I-II, ~25-35 ha including granaries and barracks) serving as 14th LE nome capital and starting point of the Ways of Horus (~5.35k NK peak).

Kom Abu Billo-Egypt.name: Kom Abu Billo
Kom Abu Billo-Egypt.evidence_basis: French archaeological mission (Dhennin) documents an Old Kingdom through Late Period western Delta desert-edge town controlling natron and salt trade from Wadi el-Natrun, reaching ~5.25k in the Saite period.

Deir el-Gabrawi-Egypt.name: Deir el-Gabrawi
Deir el-Gabrawi-Egypt.evidence_basis: 12th Upper Egyptian nome capital on the east bank north of Asyut whose 6th Dynasty nomarchal tombs (Ibi, Djau; Davies; Kanawati) attest a prominent Old Kingdom provincial center of ~5.2k.

Tod-Egypt.name: Tod
Tod-Egypt.evidence_basis: IFAO excavations (Bisson de la Roque; Pierrat-Bonnefois) uncover an Old through Late Period Montu temple town famous for the Amenemhat II Tod Treasure, housing ~4.85k-5.12k across the MK and NK.

Tell el-Yahudiya-Egypt.name: Tell el-Yahudiya
Tell el-Yahudiya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Petrie (1906) and EES Delta Survey map a ~14 ha Hyksos earth-ramparted enclosure (~3.75k in SIP) later developed by Ramesses III into a tiled palace and temple town (~4.88k).

Kom el-Hisn-Egypt.name: Kom el-Hisn
Kom el-Hisn-Egypt.evidence_basis: 3rd Lower Egyptian nome capital excavated by Wenke et al. (1988; 2016) across a ~15 ha domestic and cattle-rearing settlement mound, peaking at ~3.85k in the Old Kingdom and ~4.72k in the Middle Kingdom.

Dahshur-Egypt.name: Dahshur
Dahshur-Egypt.evidence_basis: DAI drill cores and excavations (Alexanian & Seidlmayer 2002; Love 2003) identify Snefru's 4th Dynasty valley pyramid town (at least 200x130 m core + suburbs, ~3.45k) and major 12th Dynasty expansion under Amenemhat II/III (~4.62k).

Medamud-Egypt.name: Medamud
Medamud-Egypt.evidence_basis: IFAO excavations (Bisson de la Roque; Relats Montserrat) document a substantial Montu temple town and ceramic-production hub 5.6 km NE of Karnak spanning OK through Late Period (~3.85k-4.58k).

Medinet Madi-Egypt.name: Medinet Madi
Medinet Madi-Egypt.evidence_basis: University of Pisa excavations (Bresciani; Giammarusti) uncover the 12th Dynasty Renenutet/Sobek temple foundation of Amenemhat III (~2.45k) expanding into a larger southwestern Fayum agricultural town (~4.54k by Saite times).

Meidum-Egypt.name: Meidum
Meidum-Egypt.evidence_basis: 4th Dynasty pyramid settlement and elite mastaba zone of Snefru (Petrie; Rowe; Moeller 2016) peaking near 4.51k during construction before persisting as a stable agricultural town south of Itjtawy (~2.7k-3.2k).

Balat-Egypt.name: Balat
Balat-Egypt.evidence_basis: IFAO excavations at Ayn Asil (Soukiassian; Jeuthe; Baud 1997; Moeller 2016) map a ~33 ha 6th Dynasty Dakhla Oasis governor's palace, fortified town, and pottery workshops housing ~3.8k-4.47k through the FIP/MK before shifting toward Mut.

Deir el-Bersha-Egypt.name: Deir el-Bersha
Deir el-Bersha-Egypt.evidence_basis: KU Leuven excavations (Willems) document the east-bank nomarchal seat and Hatnub-limestone quarry support settlement opposite Hermopolis, peaking near 4.42k under 12th Dynasty Hare nome governors.

Tell el-Retaba-Egypt.name: Tell el-Retaba
Tell el-Retaba-Egypt.evidence_basis: Polish-Slovak Archaeological Mission excavations (Rzepka; Hudec) map a fortified ~8-12 ha Wadi Tumilat border town with Ramesside defense walls, stables, and continuous TIP domestic quarters peaking near 4.31k.

Hawara-Egypt.name: Hawara
Hawara-Egypt.evidence_basis: 12th Dynasty pyramid and Labyrinth mortuary town of Amenemhat III on the Bahr Yussef canal (Petrie; Uytterhoeven), housing ~4.24k workers, priests, and administrators during construction before settling at ~1.8k-2.1k.

Hibis-Egypt.name: Hibis
Hibis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Administrative capital of the Southern Oasis (Kharga) centered on the 26th Dynasty Amun Temple of Hibis (Winlock; Cruz-Uribe; Giddy 1987), expanding under Saite desert investment to ~4.18k.

Tura-Egypt.name: Tura
Tura-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major royal fine-limestone quarrying town opposite Memphis attested by vast Early Dynastic Helwan-Tura cemeteries (Junker; Kohler) and Wadi al-Jarf papyri recording organized quarry gangs (~3.1k-3.96k).

Umm Mawagir-Egypt.name: Umm Mawagir
Umm Mawagir-Egypt.evidence_basis: Yale Theban Desert Road Survey excavations (Darnell & Manassa 2013) reveal a ~15-20 ha Second Intermediate Period-early New Kingdom urban provisioning hub with industrial-scale state bakeries housing ~3.89k at peak.

Mut el-Kharab-Egypt.name: Mut el-Kharab
Mut el-Kharab-Egypt.evidence_basis: Monash University excavations (Hope 2001-2016; Hubschmann 2010) document the Seth temple precinct and succeeding administrative capital of Dakhla Oasis from Old Kingdom through TIP-Saite peaks (~3.81k).

El-Bawiti-Egypt.name: El-Bawiti
El-Bawiti-Egypt.evidence_basis: Capital of the Northern Oasis (Bahariya) attested by New Kingdom governors' tombs (Amenhotep Huy) and opulent 26th Dynasty chapels and elite burials at Qasr/Ain el-Muftella (Fakhry 1942; Colin; Giddy 1987), peaking near 3.74k.

Tarkhan-Egypt.name: Tarkhan
Tarkhan-Egypt.evidence_basis: Petrie (1913-1914) excavated >2,000 Early Dynastic graves and mastabas immediately south of Memphis indicating a prosperous Dynasty 0-2 regional town of ~3.28k that declined as Old Kingdom Memphite centers consolidated.

Gebel el-Silsila-Egypt.name: Gebel el-Silsila
Gebel el-Silsila-Egypt.evidence_basis: Swedish Mission excavations (Nilsson & Ward) uncover extensive New Kingdom sandstone quarries, worker huts, and rock-cut shrines along the Nile gorge supplying Karnak and Luxor temples (~2.95k-3.21k NK workforce).

Tell el-Borg-Egypt.name: Tell el-Borg
Tell el-Borg-Egypt.evidence_basis: North Sinai Archaeological Project excavations (Hoffmeier 2014) expose successive 18th and 19th Dynasty mudbrick fortresses, moat, stables, and civilian support quarters guarding the Pelusiac mouth (~2.85k-3.15k).

Tell Ibrahim Awad-Egypt.name: Tell Ibrahim Awad
Tell Ibrahim Awad-Egypt.evidence_basis: Netherlands-Russian excavations (van Haarlem; Belova) reveal a ~10 ha eastern Delta gezira settlement with stratified Early Dynastic-Middle Kingdom temple phases and urban housing peaking near 2.65k before Avaris eclipsed it.

Amheida-Egypt.name: Amheida
Amheida-Egypt.evidence_basis: NYU excavations (Bagnall; Kaper & Demaree 2005; Hubschmann 2010) document Old Kingdom domestic ceramics, a Thoth temple, and TIP-Saite donation stelae in western Dakhla Oasis (~1.85k-2.65k in Late Pharaonic times).

Tell el-Haruba-Egypt.name: Tell el-Haruba
Tell el-Haruba-Egypt.evidence_basis: Ben-Gurion University North Sinai survey (Oren 1987; 2006) excavated a fortified Ramesside administrative compound, granaries, and industrial pottery workshops along the coastal Ways of Horus supporting ~2.15k-2.55k.

Zawiyet Umm el-Rakham-Egypt.name: Zawiyet Umm el-Rakham
Zawiyet Umm el-Rakham-Egypt.evidence_basis: University of Liverpool excavations (Snape 2003; 2013) reveal a ~2 ha 140x140 m fortified enclosure plus extramural provisioning magazines and temples built by Ramesses II 300 km west of the Delta (~1.95k-2.45k garrison and dependents).

Aghurmi-Egypt.name: Aghurmi
Aghurmi-Egypt.evidence_basis: DAI excavations on the Aghurmi acropolis (Kuhlmann 1988; Fakhry 1973) date the Amun Oracle temple and fortified Siwa oasis citadel to the 26th Dynasty under Amasis, supporting ~1.95k-2.41k oasis inhabitants and temple staff.

Wadi al-Jarf-Egypt.name: Wadi al-Jarf
Wadi al-Jarf-Egypt.evidence_basis: French-Egyptian excavations (Tallet & Marouard 2014) uncover 30 rock-cut boat galleries, an artificial L-shaped mole, administrative camps, and Merer's papyri showing massive 4th Dynasty rotational port crews (~1.95k-2.35k).

Mersa Gawasis-Egypt.name: Mersa Gawasis
Mersa Gawasis-Egypt.evidence_basis: BU-Naples excavations (Bard & Fattovich 2007-2018) expose ship-storage galleries, anchors, and Vizier Antefoker's stela documenting 3,756 expedition personnel, indicating a 12th Dynasty seasonal port population averaging ~1.85k-2.3k.

Kuban-Egypt.name: Kuban
Kuban-Egypt.evidence_basis: Emery & Kirwan (1935) and Vogel (2004) map a ~4 ha Middle and New Kingdom fortified Nile stronghold guarding the Wadi Allaqi gold-mining tracks, housing ~1.45k-2.25k soldiers, miners, and local dependents.

Minshat Abu Omar-Egypt.name: Minshat Abu Omar
Minshat Abu Omar-Egypt.evidence_basis: Munich East Delta Expedition (Kroeper & Wildung 1994) excavated >420 Predynastic-Early Dynastic graves with Levantine imports on a Pelusiac gezira (~2.15k ED trade hub), plus Late Period reoccupation (~1.65k).

Ayn Sokhna-Egypt.name: Ayn Sokhna
Ayn Sokhna-Egypt.evidence_basis: IFAO-Sorbonne excavations (Abd el-Raziq; Tallet 2012) map a ~15 ha Red Sea harbor, 9 storage galleries, and copper-smelting furnaces with stelae recording 3,000-4,000-man Sinai/Punt expeditions (~1.45k-2.12k operational base).

Roman Bath of Ptolemy XII Auletes-Egypt.name: Roman Bath of Ptolemy XII Auletes

Qasr Ibrim-Egypt.name: Qasr Ibrim
Qasr Ibrim-Egypt.evidence_basis: EES excavations (Horton; Rose; Adams) document a fortified cliff-top Lower Nubian citadel established c. 1000 BC with a 25th Dynasty Taharqa temple and massive mudbrick fortifications housing ~1.65k-1.95k.

Area of Tombs of Ankhtifi and Sebekhotep.name: Area of Tombs of Ankhtifi and Sebekhotep

Tell el-Farkha-Egypt.name: Tell el-Farkha
Tell el-Farkha-Egypt.evidence_basis: Polish Archaeological Expedition (Chlodnicki; Cialowicz 2012; Moeller 2016) excavated 4.5 ha across three koms with administrative compounds, breweries, and mastabas peaking near 1.9k in Dynasty 0-1 before abandonment c. 2600 BC.

Bir el-Abd-Egypt.name: Bir el-Abd
Bir el-Abd-Egypt.evidence_basis: North Sinai Survey excavations (Oren 1987) uncovered a ~1.5 ha 18th-19th Dynasty fortified waystation, 40x40 m brick fortress, four massive vaulted granaries, and adjacent water-reservoir settlement (~1.25k-1.85k).

Qasr el-Sagha-Egypt.name: Qasr el-Sagha
Qasr el-Sagha-Egypt.evidence_basis: DAI-Krakow excavations (Sliwa 1992; Moeller 2016) map a ~2.5 ha walled orthogonal Middle Kingdom town (114x80 m with ~30 standardized five-room barrack houses plus western hamlet) housing ~1.45k-1.7k quarry workers and guards.

Philae-Egypt.name: Philae
Philae-Egypt.evidence_basis: Southern First Cataract island shrine and frontier settlement attested from 25th-26th Dynasty shrines of Taharqa, Psamtik II, and Amasis (Haeny; Baines & Malek 2000), supporting ~1k-1.65k priests, boatmen, and guards.

Serabit el-Khadim-Egypt.name: Serabit el-Khadim
Serabit el-Khadim-Egypt.evidence_basis: Petrie (1906) and Valbelle & Bonnet (1996) document the highland Hathor temple, turquoise mines, stone miner camps, and >400 expedition stelae recording 500-1,500-strong MK-NK seasonal mining communities.

Qasr el-Farafra-Egypt.name: Qasr el-Farafra
Qasr el-Farafra-Egypt.evidence_basis: Smallest Western Desert oasis attested as Ta-iht ('Land of the Cow') from Dynasty V through New Kingdom and Saite texts (Giddy 1987; Hubschmann 2010), sustaining a modest spring-fed oasis community of ~650-1,450.

Wadi Maghara-Egypt.name: Wadi Maghara
Wadi Maghara-Egypt.evidence_basis: Old and Middle Kingdom South Sinai turquoise and copper mining settlement with fortified stone ridge-top miners' village (~125 huts mapped by Petrie 1906; Tallet), accommodating ~950-1,350 expedition personnel.

Tell Ras Budran-Egypt.name: Tell Ras Budran
Tell Ras Budran-Egypt.evidence_basis: University of Toronto excavations (Mumford 2006) uncover a ~2 ha fortified limestone coastal stronghold and anchorage on the El-Markha plain linking Wadi al-Jarf to Sinai mines (~850-1,150 late OK garrison and transit hub).

Deir el-Medina-Egypt.name: Deir el-Medina
Deir el-Medina-Egypt.evidence_basis: IFAO excavations and ostraca archives (Bruyere; Cerny; Bierbrier; Kemp 2006) document 68 walled dwellings within ~2 ha plus ~50 extramural huts housing 60-120 royal tomb artisans and their families (~420-630 total) until abandonment c. 1060 BC.
